question.worked_solution:
First, we drop the parentheses and the addition sign, which gives

$$
\text{ }-\frac{1}{11}+(-\frac{3}{11})=-\frac{1}{11}-\frac{3}{11}.
$$

 

Now, since both fractions have a common denominator of $11$, we can combine the numerators, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{11}-\frac{3}{11} & =\frac{-1-3}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we work out $-1-3$ using our number line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14149424/assets/64d008419fd882c918e73b577956b3e36d3a32814fff62d495c0f75b7d107cd1.png)

We find that $-1-3=-4.$ So, we get

$$
\frac{-1-3}{11}=\frac{-4}{11}=-\frac{4}{11}.
$$
